notes: Primary problem: queue backpressure causes SLA misses during incident bursts; manual scale-up is slow.
They currently run agent-assist and ticket summarization on-prem (proprietary model) but want better cost/latency.
Quote from CTO: "We can tolerate short tail latency spikes but not >2% SLA failures during Black Friday window."
Interested in Redwood's KV/prefix caching + intelligent batching to reduce token cost without raising latency.
Request: deterministic routing to dedicated pool for VIP accounts, fallback to lower-cost models for bulk traffic; need canary rollouts and automatic fallback.
Integration stack: Zendesk + Genesys voice; tool-calling required for zendesktrigger and crm_write endpoints.
Legal: data residency must stay in us-east for PII; 90-day retention for transcripts; logs exported to their SIEM via syslog.
POC success metrics: sustained 600 concurrent, p95 latency <250ms for agent assist, <10ms added overhead on tool-calls, no more than 1% error/failure under 3x bursts.
use_case_summary: Workloads: real-time agent_assist (low-latency streaming), ticket_summarization (batch), reranking for suggested replies, tool_calling (CRM actions).
Targets: baseline 200 concurrent agents; ensure headroom to 3x baseline for incident bursts and seasonal peaks.
Model preferences: prefer open Llama-variants or tuned customer models; accept quantized variants as fallback.
Routing needs: deterministic VIP routing, autoscaling for non-VIP, cross-region failover, canary deploys.
Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, SOC 2 and audit logs, US data residency.
